title: Integer `%` never overflows
verdict: no overflow at any width; `MIN % -1` is 0
description: `%` on integers has no overflowing input. The kernel takes `wrapping_rem` and, when the remainder is nonzero and its sign differs from the divisor's, adds the divisor: the sum lies strictly between 0 and the divisor, so it fits. `MIN % -1` is 0 (`wrapping_rem`), and a literal divisor of ±1 fills 0. One macro instantiates the kernels for `Int8` to `Int64`, so every width behaves the same. The floor remainder and NULL for a zero divisor are in polars-int-modulus.
reference: `modulus` on integers is the truncated remainder (`Int.tmod`), which never overflows either; `MIN % -1` is 0 (`min_mod_neg_one`).

evidence.note: A literal divisor: the remainder of the absolute values, below |divisor|, with the divisor's sign.
`impl_signed_arith_kernel!` for i8, i16, i32, i64, i128.

notes: The kernels are one generic macro, so the reading covers i8 to i64. The adjustment `mod_ += other` only runs when the remainder and the divisor have opposite signs, where the sum cannot overflow. The wheels build without `overflow-checks` (polars-int-arith), so the wrapping operations cannot panic either.
Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3). The streaming engine evaluates expressions through polars-expr on each morsel (crates/polars-stream/src/expression.rs), so these kernels serve both engines.
